source: RFC 5869 — HMAC-based Extract-and-Expand Key Derivation Function (HKDF) (Krawczyk & Eronen, IETF, May 2010)
section: Appendix A, Test Cases 1–3 ("Basic test case with SHA-256", "Test with SHA-256 and longer inputs/outputs", "Test with SHA-256 and zero-length salt/info") — the RFC's SHA-1 test cases (A.4–A.7) are out of scope for FedOS and are not imported.

notes: Verbatim import (Stage 73). The RFC prints each field as '0x'-prefixed hex, wrapped across multiple lines with a trailing '(N octets)' annotation; this file concatenates the wrapped hex into one lowercase string per field and drops the '0x' prefix and the octet-count annotation — a minimal, non-value-altering formatting change, byte-length-checked against the RFC's own stated octet counts for every field in every case. RFC 5869 does not publish an explicit 'wrong info/salt must not match' negative vector, but Test Case 1 and Test Case 3 share the exact same IKM (0x0b0b...0b, 22 octets) while using different salt/info (Test Case 1: real salt+info; Test Case 3: zero-length salt+info) and produce different OKM — this is an intrinsic property of the two official vectors placed side by side, not a fabricated case, and it is the domain-separation proof required by docs/crypto_vector_sources.md §6. No Rust code reads this file yet.

vectors.description: Test Case 1 — basic test case with SHA-256.
Test Case 2 — SHA-256 with longer inputs/outputs (80-octet IKM/salt/info, L=82).
Test Case 3 — SHA-256 with zero-length salt and zero-length info; same IKM as Test Case 1.
vectors.notes: salt is a zero-length octet string; per RFC 5869 §2.2 a zero-length or absent salt is internally replaced with HashLen (32) zero octets before HMAC-extract — the salt field here is intentionally empty, not omitted.
